prompt:
I need the front end for Heirloom Kitchen. A personal tool where a home cook directs an AI model to transcribe, standardize, and organize scanned family recipes into a printable cookbook, while checking each result against the original handwriting.

Who's using it: Ben Szabo, 36, a software tester who is making a cookbook of his late grandmother Ilona's Hungarian recipes as a Christmas gift for his mother and two aunts. He cooks a little, reads no Hungarian beyond food words, and works on this on weekend evenings.

What they're doing right now: On Saturday afternoon he gave the AI its brief: transcribe every scanned recipe, translate the Hungarian notes, convert dekagrams and 'one glass' measures to cups and grams with the originals kept, and group recipes into chapters. It has finished 41 of 63 recipes and paused on 7 where it isn't confident, including a smudged quantity in 'Diós beigli' and a 'Mama's way' note it can't interpret. Ben is going through its work now. He is comparing transcriptions to the scans, approving good ones, correcting the AI where it guessed wrong, and deciding whether to tell it to keep 'one glass' as a 250 ml water glass for the remaining recipes before it continues.

What's in the system at this point: 63 scanned recipes (photos of handwritten slips and notebook pages, 1958–1994), 41 transcribed, 7 flagged low-confidence, 15 not started. For each: original scan, AI transcription, translation, converted ingredient quantities with originals (e.g. '25 dkg flour → 250 g / 2 cups'), confidence per line, AI's stated assumptions ('assumed "glass" = 200 ml'), Ben's status (approved, edited, needs aunt's input). Proposed chapters: Soups (8), Mains (17), Pastries & Cakes (24), Preserves (9), Other (5). 12 recipes approved so far; Ben has edited 4. Gift deadline: print order by Dec 10.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
